text:
Aisha: hi team, onboarding hit a snag. I'm on a rental apartment ISP and when connected to the split-tunnel VPN I can't reach our internal docs site at 10.41.2.22. Browser times out, curl fails. On macOS Ventura, WireGuard app. Anyone know quick fixes?

Tom (Networking): welcome Aisha! Common culprit is CG-NAT or the ISP refusing hairpin to RFC1918. Can you share `route get 10.41.2.22` and `ifconfig` output and whether the WireGuard interface is utun or wg0?

Aisha: pasted minimal output:
$ route get 10.41.2.22
10.41.2.22 via 100.64.0.1 dev en0 src 192.168.0.22

$ ifconfig | grep -A3 utun
utun2: flags=8051<UP,POINTOPOINT,RUNNING,MULTICAST> mtu 1380

Tom (Networking): yep 100.64.x.x indicates CG-NAT. Two fast options: 1) add host route to force that internal prefix over utun2: `sudo route -n add -net 10.41.0.0/16 -interface utun2` OR 2) use SSH port forward via bastion: `ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_rdw -L 8080:10.41.2.22:80 rdw-bastion` then open http://localhost:8080.

Nora (SRE): seconding Tom. For reproducibility we'll add a note in the new-hire checklist. Also watch out for DNS: if the client still tries to resolve public names, try `dscacheutil -flushcache` and ensure the VPN sets the search domain. If you need full-tunnel for the first week we can temporarily enable it on your account.

Aisha: used the ssh -L forward, docs load fine. Thanks! can we add the utun route command to the checklist for Mac folks?

Tom (Networking): will do and I'll add a tiny helper script that detects 100.64.0.0/10 as next-hop and prints the recommended `route` command for the utun interface.

Infra Bot: Created INF-660: "New-hire helper: detect CG-NAT and recommend utun route on macOS" assigned to Networking.

Aisha: great, leaving this thread for others who hit flaky home ISPs. Appreciate the quick help :)
